literature_notes: L1 (PMID 10336468) reports an epitope-tagged CA14 construct expressed in COS-7 cells that localises to the plasma membrane and retains CA enzymatic activity in the membrane fraction. However, the paper names neither the tag type nor the tag position (N-terminal, C-terminal, or internal), and it does not state that the tag is on the extracellular face. CA14 is a type I single-pass membrane protein with exactly one extracellular terminus (mature N-terminus, residue 16, after SP cleavage at residue 15) and a short intracellular C-tail (residues 313–337). A C-terminal intracellular epitope tag would produce identical plasma-membrane localisation data, so the topology-derived rule ('exactly one extracellular terminus, therefore the tag is there') cannot be applied with confidence — the tag could equally be intracellular. Applying the 'doubt the evidence → drop the site' rule, no surface tag site is proposed. No other ledger lines are provided.
